assets.notes: far valley, the core (r under 850): the heart and the Iris meadow, for views from the valley sides when the heart is not streamed in. OPTIONAL: leave it out and the file is exactly the ring r 850-2750. Its rim is the ring's inner rim (the same vertices), so the two join without a gap.

notes: A low-poly copy of Map 1's valley for the view where voxel terrain is not streamed in: a decimated height field on a polar grid (2-degree steps; cells about 30 studs at r 850 growing to 64 x 96 at the rim, r 2,750; the vertices are nudged off the exact grid so that patches of a class do not show as rectangles from the horn). The ground is a LOWER ENVELOPE of Map1_Height.png: at every 4-stud sample it lies at least 6 studs under the lowest of that sample and its eight neighbours, so real terrain covers it wherever terrain is present ('fit' gives the measured depths). Tiles: M1_Far_A1 ... M1_Far_C3 are a 3 x 3 grid over the ring (column A west to C east, row 1 north to 3 south); M1_Far_Core is the disc inside r 850 and is optional. Parts: M1_Far_<tile>_<class>, one flat colour per part, the palette's own (Map1_Terrain.json 'palette'), the same in every tile. Ground classes (Grass, DryGrass, Heather, Rock, Scree, Water) are smooth-shaded with normals worked out on the whole sheet before it was cut (faces that meet at over 45 degrees keep an edge), so parts and tiles shade as one surface; Water is the lake's bed in the lake's colour (the bed, not the surface, so that it stays under the real lake). Canopy is a separate flat-shaded sheet at least 18 studs above the true ground (18-24 on even ground) wherever the conifers are dense; it has no sides and faces up only, so from under it, among the real trees, it is not drawn. No vertex colours, no textures, single-sided, every triangle faces up. Every asset of this file is modelled in world space with its pivot at the map centre (0, 0, 0): place each at position (0, 0, 0) with yaw 0. In the file the assets stand in a row along +X, as in every other GLB of this project; 'origin' is each asset's pivot in the file. Each part also carries 'position' and 'size': the centre and the extent of its bounding box in Roblox world space once its asset stands at the map centre. A MeshPart's Position is its bounding box's centre, so a part is in place when its Position equals 'position' and its Size equals 'size' (after the importer's own turn about Y has been undone, as for every other asset). Set RenderFidelity to Precise: neighbouring parts share an edge exactly, and a part simplified on its own could open a crack along it. CanCollide, CanQuery, CanTouch and CastShadow are false; the model is Persistent.

grid.partRule: a triangle belongs to the tile its centroid lies in; a ground class with under 24 triangles in a tile (Scree: under 8) takes that tile's commonest other ground class

colourNote: To match the real terrain exactly at the streaming edge, give the Grass and DryGrass parts the colour the terrain's Grass material ends up with; the palette values here are the Blender paint's (meadow and dry).
